limit_order_match_processing.meaning: a limit order matching (partial or full) is being processed through _processLimitBidOrder or _processLimitAskOrder
limit_order_match_processing.checkpoint: before the zero-cost check during limit order matching

matched_amounts_disjoint_bits.meaning: the matched base amount and matched quote amount have no overlapping 1-bits (e.g., base = 256 and quote in 1..255, or 40 & 21)
matched_amounts_disjoint_bits.checkpoint: before the zero-cost check during limit order matching

matched_base_amount_nonzero.meaning: the matched base amount is nonzero
matched_base_amount_nonzero.checkpoint: before the zero-cost check during limit order matching

matched_quote_amount_nonzero.meaning: the matched quote amount is nonzero
matched_quote_amount_nonzero.checkpoint: before the zero-cost check during limit order matching

rejected_as_zero_cost_trade.meaning: the legitimate limit order match is rejected as a zero-cost trade
rejected_as_zero_cost_trade.checkpoint: during limit order matching, at the zero-cost check outcome

traders_encounter_unexplained_failures.meaning: traders, especially algorithmic ones using round numbers, encounter unexplained failures
traders_encounter_unexplained_failures.checkpoint: after the limit order matching attempt

assumptions: The zero-cost check is evaluated during limit order matching and its rejection outcome is observable as a revert/failure.
Matched base and quote amounts are observable quantities at the zero-cost check checkpoint.

unresolved.description: The exact zero-cost check expression and its operands are not quoted in prose; the rejection outcome is represented as a grounded Boolean rather than a numeric relation.
Report does not specify whether matched amounts are caller-supplied inputs or derived from order state; the disjoint-bits condition is encoded as a grounded Boolean.

limitations: The impact is potential; the failure outcome is encoded as a Boolean witness rather than an inevitable effect.
The disjoint-bits precondition is represented as a single grounded Boolean because the bit-level relation is not expressible in the available predicate grammar.
Caller identity and authorization for triggering limit order matching are not stated and are not encoded.
